questions.prompt: What does fine-tuning do to a pretrained model's weights?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Answer: It continues training them on a smaller, more specific dataset

Fine-tuning continues training the same weights on new, usually much smaller and more specific, data — it doesn't discard or replace the model.
keyPoints: Fine-tuning continues training the same weights on new, usually much smaller and more specific, data — it doesn't discard or replace the model.

questions.prompt: According to widely reproduced fine-tuning findings, what usually matters more for a good result?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Answer: Data quality and consistency, even with a small dataset

A small, clean, consistent dataset routinely beats a large noisy one — fine-tuning mostly needs to demonstrate the target behavior clearly, not teach language from scratch.
keyPoints: A small, clean, consistent dataset routinely beats a large noisy one — fine-tuning mostly needs to demonstrate the target behavior clearly, not teach language from scratch.

questions.prompt: What do prefix tuning and prompt tuning train, while leaving the base model frozen?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Answer: A set of trainable 'virtual token' embeddings prepended to the input

These methods only train virtual token embeddings that get prepended to inputs, influencing what the frozen model attends to, without touching any of its weights.
keyPoints: These methods only train virtual token embeddings that get prepended to inputs, influencing what the frozen model attends to, without touching any of its weights.

questions.prompt: What is a chat template responsible for?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Answer: Converting a structured conversation (system/user/assistant turns) into the exact token format the model expects

A chat template defines the precise text/token structure — including special tokens marking role boundaries — that a model was trained to expect for conversations.
keyPoints: A chat template defines the precise text/token structure — including special tokens marking role boundaries — that a model was trained to expect for conversations.

questions.prompt: What can RLHF teach that plain SFT alone cannot?
questions.referenceAnswer: SFT only sees one correct target per example; RLHF's reward-model-plus-RL approach lets the model learn from relative comparisons between responses, closer to how humans actually judge quality.
keyPoints: SFT only sees one correct target per example; RLHF's reward-model-plus-RL approach lets the model learn from relative comparisons between responses, closer to how humans actually judge quality.

choices.text: How to tokenize input text

How to run on a GPU
How to quantize a model

questions.prompt: What is the main trade-off of PPO-based RLHF compared to DPO?
questions.referenceAnswer: PPO-based RLHF can capture more nuance through an updatable reward model, but at the cost of significant extra infrastructure, tuning effort, and instability risk compared to DPO's simpler direct approach.
keyPoints: PPO-based RLHF can capture more nuance through an updatable reward model, but at the cost of significant extra infrastructure, tuning effort, and instability risk compared to DPO's simpler direct approach.

PPO-based RLHF requires no preference data at all
There is no meaningful difference between the two

questions.prompt: What does the Trainer class primarily handle?
questions.referenceAnswer: Trainer abstracts away the loop mechanics so you configure behavior via TrainingArguments rather than hand-writing the training loop yourself.
keyPoints: Trainer abstracts away the loop mechanics so you configure behavior via TrainingArguments rather than hand-writing the training loop yourself.

choices.text: Generating training data automatically
The training loop mechanics — batching, optimizer steps, checkpointing, logging — configured via TrainingArguments
Quantizing the base model
Serving the model to end users

questions.prompt: What is a risk of repeatedly fine-tuning on top of the previous fine-tuned checkpoint across multiple rounds?
questions.referenceAnswer: Each additional fine-tuning round on top of a previous one adds more opportunity for forgetting to accumulate, which is why going back to the base model with an updated combined dataset is often more robust.
keyPoints: Each additional fine-tuning round on top of a previous one adds more opportunity for forgetting to accumulate, which is why going back to the base model with an updated combined dataset is often more robust.

choices.text: It's technically impossible to do more than once
Catastrophic forgetting risk compounds across rounds
It always improves the model with no downside
It requires deleting the original base model

questions.prompt: Fine-tuning improves training loss but degrades held-out behavior. What would you inspect first, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer: Check overfitting and train/evaluation overlap. Compare against the unchanged base model. Inspect learning rate, data quality and task-specific metrics.
keyPoints: Check overfitting and train/evaluation overlap.
Compare against the unchanged base model.
Inspect learning rate, data quality and task-specific metrics.

questions.prompt: How would you test that the change fixed this incident rather than hiding it?
questions.referenceAnswer: Keep a reproducible failing case for this incident. Inspect learning rate, data quality and task-specific metrics. Compare the same workload before and after the change; record both the target metric and regressions.
keyPoints: Inspect learning rate, data quality and task-specific metrics.
Compare the same workload before and after the change.
Check regressions as well as the target metric.

questions.prompt: The fix works in a small test but fails at production scale. What next?
questions.referenceAnswer: Check overfitting and train/evaluation overlap. Measure representative workloads and separate resource, data and configuration differences. Stage a rollout with a rollback condition and rerun the original failure case.
keyPoints: Check overfitting and train/evaluation overlap.
Measure a representative workload.
Stage rollout and define rollback criteria.
